problem: No RL navigation environment supported last-meters pedestrian navigation to a specific building entrance for blind and visually-impaired (BVI) people. Driving simulators (CARLA, AirSim, LGSVL) lack realistic buildings and scene text. Street View environments (StreetLearn, Touchdown-style) have sparse nodes about 10 m apart, a vehicle-mounted viewpoint, low-resolution imagery (1664×832), and no labels for doors, house numbers or street signs.
motivation: About 250M people are BVI. Interviews with BVI users, orientation and mobility specialists and app developers showed that GPS apps handle long-range routing, but finding the exact door in the last few meters still needs costly or slow human help (Aira, BeMyEyes). Solving this requires high-resolution, pedestrian-view imagery with scene-text labels, so an agent can learn to read house numbers and street signs while navigating.
key_idea: Build SEVN, a Gym-compatible sidewalk simulator of densely sampled (1 node/m) high-resolution 360° panoramas of Montreal's Little Italy with annotated doors, house numbers and street signs. Then train a PPO agent that fuses a low-res image, simulated GPS goal offset and (ground-truth) visible scene text, tiled as extra image channels, to navigate to a goal door.
insight: Vision is indispensable. Removing the image (NoImg) collapses success to 0.8%, below a random walk (5.7%). Image-only already reaches about 57%, and fusing GPS and visible text lifts success to 74.9%. Text alone adds little over image-only (NoGPS 58.2% vs ImgOnly 57.%), so most of the gain comes from GPS combined with image and text. Heavy GPS noise (σ=25, 100 m) degrades performance to about NoGPS level, while small noise barely matters (figure only). The learned policies essentially memorize the training region: the Small-trained agent gets 1.0% on Large, and even a 20M-frame Large-trained agent only reaches 21.1% on Large. The simple tiled-CNN fusion therefore does not learn transferable reading-based navigation.
method: SEVN data capture: 360° video with a Vuze+ stereo rig held above head height. Poses come from ORB-SLAM2 on the undistorted front-left camera. The graph is sparsified to 1 node per meter and hand-curated. Panoramas are 3840×1280 after cropping, about 3.5× StreetLearn's pixel count. Totals: 4,988 panoramas over about 6.3 km, split into Large (3,831 images) and Small (1,157 images, 116 unique goal doors).

Annotations: bounding boxes with ground-truth text for house numbers and street-name signs, plus polygons for doors with clearly associated house numbers (1,303 door, 213 sign and 1,743 house-number annotations). Faces and plates are blurred.

Gym simulator: discrete actions are ±22.5° and ±67.5° turns plus forward to the neighbor node nearest the current heading (no move if none within ±45°); some tasks add 'read' and 'done'. The agent observes an 84×84 RGB crop (about 135–140° FOV) of the low-res panorama. GT text labels fully inside the FOV are passed as encoded observations. Runs at 400–800 FPS on 2 CPU cores.

Oracle and tasks: a NetworkX shortest-path oracle over (node, 22.5° heading) poses. Success means reaching the node nearest the goal door with the door polygon fully in the FOV. Eight tasks are defined: modality ablations AllObs/NoImg/NoGPS/ImgOnly, Intersection, CostlyTxt, Sparse and Explorer (multi-goal). Rewards come in dense, costly-read, sparse and multi-goal variants.

Observation encoding: the GPS input is the goal offset (absolute and relative) scaled to [-1,1]. Each house number is 4 one-hot digits (40-d), with up to 3 stacked (120-d); street names are an 11-way one-hot.

Fusion policy: each non-image modality is tiled into a (1,w,w) plane and concatenated with RGB into an (8,w,w) tensor (missing modalities are zero-filled). The network is 3 conv layers followed by a dense-256 layer (ReLU) with an actor softmax and a critic value head. It is trained with PPO using Atari-style hyperparameters (lr 3e-4, 2048 steps, 4 epochs, 32 minibatches, clip 0.2) for 2M frames.

setting.backbone: small 3-conv-layer CNN + 256-unit dense actor-critic, trained from scratch with PPO
setting.model_size: not reported (3 conv layers + 256-d dense layer)
setting.training_data: PPO experience in SEVN: 2M frames on the Small split (1,157 panoramas, 116 goal doors), 10 seeds. The generalization model uses 20M frames on the Large split (3,831 panoramas). No external data.
setting.observation: 84×84 egocentric RGB crop (~135° FOV) of a real 360° panorama + simulated GPS goal offset (2-D relative / absolute, scaled to [-1,1]) + ground-truth visible scene text (house numbers, street-sign names) as one-hot vectors
setting.action_space: discrete on panorama graph: forward to nearest neighbor node (~1 m), slight turns ±22.5°, sharp turns ±67.5° (plus 'read' in CostlyTxt and 'done' in Sparse task)
setting.simulator: SEVN (OpenAI Gym env over real 360° panoramas of Little Italy, Montreal)
setting.privileged: ground-truth scene-text annotations (house numbers / street names) given as observations instead of OCR; noise-free simulated GPS offset to goal; goal on the same street segment as the start

There is no held-out split: the main evaluation is on episodes sampled in the training region.
results: On the Small street-segment door-finding task, the fused AllObs PPO agent reaches 74.9% success (best seed 85%) with a mean of 113.7 steps. This beats NoGPS (58.2%), ImgOnly (57.%), NoImg (0.8%) and a random walk (5.7%), against an oracle at 100% with 80.8 steps. Generalization fails: the Small-trained agent gets 1.0% on the unseen Large region, and a Large-trained agent with 20M frames only reaches 21.1% on Large.
limitations: Assumes ground-truth scene-text labels as input rather than a real OCR/detection pipeline, so reading difficulty is sidestepped.
Policies do not generalize beyond the training region (1.0% on unseen streets). Evaluation is on the training region itself, with a single neighborhood of about 6 km and a tiny CNN.
Most defined tasks (Intersection, Sparse, CostlyTxt, Explorer) have no reported results. Two degenerate seeds were removed for AllObs. Real-world and edge deployment is not addressed.
